title: Moral Consumers and the Environment
abstract: arXiv:2611.09515v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the taxation of environmentally harmful goods when consumers have a Kantian desire to ``do the right thing''. A consumer evaluates her buying strategy, a rule that specifies whether to buy, by the material payoff she would obtain if others followed the same rule with a probability given by her degree of morality. Equilibrium exists and is unique in finite populations with heterogeneous morality. The optimal tax depends crucially on whether consumers are aware that tax revenue is returned to them. If they are, the Pigovian tax is optimal under homogeneous morality, whatever consumers know about environmental costs, and we give conditions under which it remains the unique optimum under heterogeneous morality. If they are not, the optimal tax is lower, and more so the more moral consumers are. translated_abstract: 我们研究了当消费者具有康德式的“做正确之事”的愿望时，对环境有害商品的征税问题。消费者通过比较假如他人以与其道德程度相应的概率遵循同一规则时她所能获得的物质收益，来评价自己的购买策略（即规定是否购买的规则）。在道德异质的有限人口中，均衡存在且唯一。最优税收关键取决于消费者是否意识到税收收入会返还给他们。如果意识到，那么在道德同质的情况下，无论消费者对环境成本的认知如何，庇古税都是最优的；我们还给出了在道德异质情况下庇古税仍是唯一最优解的条件。如果消费者没有意识到，最优税收会更低，且消费者道德水平越高，税收越低。在诸如欧盟碳排放交易体系这类配额制度下，任何至少与庇古配额同等严格的上限都存在均衡……
tldr: 该论文研究了具有康德式道德偏好的消费者对环境有害商品征税的影响，发现当消费者知晓税收会返还给自己时庇古税最优，而不知晓时最优税率应低于庇古税，且消费者道德水平越高税率应越低。
en_tdlr: This paper studies the taxation of environmentally harmful goods with Kantian consumers, showing that the Pigovian tax is optimal when consumers know tax revenue is rebated to them, while the optimal tax falls below the Pigovian level—by more the more moral consumers are—when they do not.
